title: Failover
subtitle: Automated traffic shifting across Active-Passive and Active-Active nodes, AZs, and regions.

sections.heading: 1. Architectural Fundamentals & Core Mechanics
sections.body: Failover is the operational mechanism of detecting a failed component and redirecting traffic to a healthy redundant instance. In **Active-Passive** failover, a primary node serves writes while one or more standby replicas receive synchronous or asynchronous replication. In **Active-Active** failover, multiple nodes or regions actively serve traffic simultaneously; if Region US-East-1 fails, global routing (Route 53 / BGP Anycast) drains traffic to US-West-2.
bullets: **Core Architectural Principle**: Failover efficacy is measured by **RTO** (Recovery Time Objective: downtime duration) and **RPO** (Recovery Point Objective: maximum data lost).
**Problem Space & Invariants**: Split-brain occurs when an isolated primary continues accepting writes after a standby is promoted; prevent it using Fencing Tokens and Quorum Leases.
**System Boundary**: Operates across client network dispatch, gateway queuing, thread execution pools, and persistent storage I/O.

sections.heading: 2. Architectural Patterns & Implementation Topologies
sections.body: Distributed architectures apply specific implementation patterns and topologies for Failover:
bullets: **Active-Passive Multi-Region (Hot Standby)**: Provides avoids cross-region multi-master write conflicts; straightforward single-writer consistency. Best suited for Relational financial databases, transactional core ledgers, and compliance-bound workloads.

**Active-Active Multi-Region**: Provides near-zero rto (instant traffic shift), lower user latency via geo-proximity routing, and active validation of all regions. Best suited for Global Tier-0 consumer apps (каталог browsing, messaging, ride-hailing, social feeds).
**RTO (Recovery Time Objective)**: How long it takes to detect failure, promote the standby, and reroute traffic (e.g., DNS TTL + health check interval).
**RPO (Recovery Point Objective)**: How many seconds of committed writes can be lost during an unplanned failover (`RPO = 0` requires synchronous or quorum replication).
**Pre-Warm Standbys**: Continuously replay read shadow traffic or replicate cache invalidations/updates to the standby region so caches stay warm.

**Over-Provision Surviving Zones**: In a 3-AZ deployment, each AZ must be provisioned at $\le 66\%$ peak utilization so losing 1 AZ brings the remaining 2 AZs to $\sim 100\%$ rather than overloading them.

sections.heading: 3. Production Strengths: Where & How to Apply
sections.body: Production deployments apply Failover across targeted operational scenarios:
bullets: **Where to Use: High-Impact Scenarios**: Optimal for Relational financial databases, transactional core ledgers, and compliance-bound workloads, suited for environments requiring Avoids cross-region multi-master write conflicts; straightforward single-writer consistency.

**Where to Use: High-Throughput Scenarios**: Recommended for Global Tier-0 consumer apps (каталог browsing, messaging, ride-hailing, social feeds), where Near-zero RTO (instant traffic shift), lower user latency via geo-proximity routing, and active validation of all regions.
**How to Use: Engineering Implementation**: Two classic failure modes derail automated failovers in production. Always establish explicit thresholds, measurement baselines, and automated monitoring.
**Architectural Leverage**: Provides predictable resource boundaries, bounds blast radius, and optimizes cost per transaction.

sections.heading: 4. Failure Modes & Trade-Offs: When to Avoid
sections.body: Improper implementation of Failover introduces operational bottlenecks and failure modes:
bullets: **Where to Avoid: Trade-Off Bottlenecks**: Avoid when constraints cannot tolerate: passive region compute sits partially idle; nonzero rto (seconds to minutes) and potential rpo > 0 if replication is async.

**Where to Avoid: Complexity Ceiling**: Avoid when operational requirements do not justify: requires conflict-free data models (crdts, last-write-wins, or home-region user pinning) and complex cross-region replication.
**Catastrophic Failure Modes**: Uncalibrated parameters can trigger queue exhaustion, thread starvation, cascading retry storms, and tail latency amplification.
**Operational Overhead**: Requires continuous observability (p95/p99 latency tracking, saturation alerts, and distributed tracing across hop boundaries).

sections.heading: 5. Staff+ Engineering Verdict & Interview Playbook
sections.body: Technical guidelines and evaluation criteria for Failover:
bullets: **Staff+ Golden Rule**: A standby cluster that sits at 0% traffic (cold cache, unscaled pools) often crashes immediately under 100% failover load unless capacity is pre-warmed.

**Staff+ Interview Playbook**: When proposing a multi-AZ or multi-region failover in an interview, always state the **headroom math** (e.g., 3 AZs running at $\le 60\%$ CPU so any 2 AZs can absorb 100% of traffic) and how you prevent **Split-Brain (Fencing Tokens)**.
